{{Short description|74th season of the National Hurling League}} {{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}} {{Infobox GAA League |league = 2005 National Hurling League |image = |dates = 20 February – 7 May 2005 |teams = 32 |team1 = Kilkenny |captain1 = [[Peter Barry (hurler)|Peter Barry]] |manager1 = [[Brian Cody]] |titles = 12th |team2 = Clare |captain2 = [[Seánie McMahon]] |manager2 = [[Anthony Daly (hurler)|Anthony Daly]] |two= Offaly |three = Mayo |threes=Longford |previous = [[2004 National Hurling League|2004]] |next = [[2006 National Hurling League|2006]] }} The '''2005 National Hurling League''', known for sponsorship reasons as the '''[[Allianz]] National Hurling League''', was the 74th edition of the [[National Hurling League]] (NHL), an annual [[hurling]] competition for the [[GAA county teams]]. [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] won the league, beating [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the final.{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/general/leagues/nhlrecords.aspx|title=National Hurling League Results 1925-2009|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=18 April 2011|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100805063526/http://www.hoganstand.com/general/leagues/nhlrecords.aspx|archivedate=5 August 2010}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/regionals/sligochampion/sport/other-sports/hurling-league-fixtures-27552939.html|title=Hurling League fixtures|website=independent}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-football/gaelic-games-scoreboard-25913635.html|title=GAELIC GAMES SCOREBOARD|website=independent}} An experimental rule was trialled in the 2005 NHL, with two points being awarded for a point scored directly from a sideline cut.{{Cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-30831070.html|title=Two points for a sideline cut on the wishlist for inter-county hurlers|date=March 6, 2018|website=Irish Examiner}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.balls.ie/gaa/stats-strengthen-two-points-sideline-cut-argument-394599|title=The Stats That Strengthen The Two Points For A Sideline Cut Argument|first=Maurice|last=Brosnan|website=Balls.ie}} ==Structure== ===Division 1=== There are 12 teams in Division 1, divided into 1A and 1B. Each team plays all the others in its group once, earning 2 points for a win and 1 for a draw. *The top three in 1A and 1B advance to Division 1 Section 1. *The bottom three in 1A and 1B go into the Division 1 Section 2. Each team in Section 1 plays the other three teams that it did not play in the first five games. The top two teams go into the NHL final – only points earned in these last three games count. Each team in Section 2 plays the other three teams that it did not play in the first five games. The bottom team is relegated – only points earned in these last three games count. ===Division 2=== There are 10 teams in Division 2, divided into 2A and 2B. Each team plays all the others in its group once, earning 2 points for a win and 1 for a draw. *The top three in 2A and 2B advance to the Division 2 Section 1. *The bottom two in 2A and 2B go into the Division 2 Section 2. Each team in Section 1 plays the other three teams that it did not play in the first four games. The top two teams go into the Division 2 final – only points earned in these last three games count. Final winners are promoted. Each team in Section 2 plays the other two teams that it did not play in the first four games. The bottom team is relegated – only points earned in these last two games count. ===Division 3=== There are 10 teams in Division 3, divided into 3A and 3B. Each team plays all the others in its group once, earning 2 points for a win and 1 for a draw. *The top three in 3A and 3B advance to the Division 3 Section 1. *The bottom two in 3A and 3B go into the Division 3 Section 2. Each team in Section 1 plays the other three teams that it did not play in the first four games. The top two teams go into the Division 3 final – only points earned in these last three games count. Final winners are promoted. Each team in Section 2 plays the other two teams that it did not play in the first four games. The top two play the Division 3 Shield Final. ==Overview== ===Division 1=== [[Brian Cody]] won his third league title in four seasons with [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]], as 'the Cats' recorded just a single defeat in the entire league. [[Clare GAA|Clare]], who were league runners-up, also suffered just one defeat in the group stages, however, they fell to Kilkenny in the final. Down at the other end of the table, [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]] and [[Down GAA|Down]] went through the group stages without a single victory. A relegation group of six teams meant that 'the Dubs' ended up at the bottom and faced relegation for the following season. ===Division 2=== [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] won the Division 2 title after recording just one defeat throughout the group stages, thus returning to the top flight having been relegated the previous year. Runners-up [[Carlow GAA|Carlow]] also faced only one defeat throughout the group stages until the last day of the league when they were defeated in the final by Offaly. Going down were [[Sligo GAA|Sligo]] who only had a draw with [[Wicklow GAA|Wicklow]] to show for their entire campaign. ===Division 3=== [[Mayo GAA|Mayo]] and [[Donegal GAA|Donegal]] qualified for the league final in this division with Mayo winning promotion. [[Cavan GAA|Cavan]], having failed to win a single game in the group stage, finished bottom of Division 3B and could thus be regarded as the worst team of all the divisions. ==Division 1== {{Infobox football league season |competition=[[National Hurling League|National Hurling League Division 1]] |season=2005 |winners=[[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]]

[[Down GAA|Down]] entered Division 1 as the promoted team. On 2 May 2005, [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] won the title following a 3-20 to 0-15 win over [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the final.{{cite web|url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/cats-send-out-warning-in-final-200720.html|title=Cats send out warning in final|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=2 May 2005|accessdate=26 April 2017}} It was their first league title since [[2003 National Hurling League|2003]] and their 12th National League title overall. [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]], who lost all of their group stage matches, were relegated from Division 1 after losing all of their matches in the relegation group. [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] won Division 2 and secured promotion to the top tier.
